title: Segregation, Recombination, Heterozygosity and Progeny Testing

content.overview: Cannabis breeding families can display substantial variation because alleles segregate and recombine and because many parents are highly heterozygous. The phenotype of one selected plant is therefore an observation about that individual, not a complete prediction of what it will transmit.

vocabulary.definition: Separation of alleles into gametes and offspring during sexual reproduction.
Formation of new combinations of genetic variants through meiotic chromosome exchange and assortment.
The expected contribution of an individual’s genetics to offspring performance for a defined trait and population.

sections.title: Siblings can differ for biological reasons
sections.body: Recombination and segregation create different allele combinations among siblings, especially from heterozygous parents. Environmental differences can add further phenotypic variation.

sections.title: Complex traits are not single-gene stories
sections.body: Many agronomic traits involve multiple loci and genotype-by-environment effects, so simple dominant/recessive expectations should not be applied without evidence that the trait follows such inheritance.

sections.title: Progeny testing asks what the parent transmits
sections.body: Evaluating offspring families can reveal whether a selected parent repeatedly contributes the desired phenotype and whether undesirable traits segregate with it.

workedExamples: A highly aromatic plant may produce a wide range of aroma profiles in offspring if the underlying trait is complex and the parent remains heterozygous.
A parent that looks average but produces consistently strong progeny may have greater breeding value for the target program than a single exceptional but inconsistent parent.
commonMistakes: Assuming a selected phenotype breeds true.
Calling every visible ratio Mendelian without sufficient population data.
Discarding family-level results in favor of one standout individual.
content.practicalApplication: For each selected parent, compare the distribution of target traits in its progeny with other families under comparable conditions and record both mean performance and variation.
content.summary: Selection becomes breeding evidence only when transmission is measured. Segregation and recombination make progeny testing central to line development.
